title: T47 connectors: agent-core requirement as a range, not a stale pin (0.5.1)
head: t47-agent-core-range
body:
## What

`connectors`' `pyproject.toml` pinned its runtime requirement on `agent-core`
to an exact version, `agent-core==0.4.0`. That's now a range with a floor and
a ceiling: `agent-core>=0.4.0,<0.8`. The `[tool.uv.sources]` entry for this
repo's own dev/test env still points at the vendored `agent-core` 0.4.0
wheel, so connectors' own tests keep running against the floor version.
Version 0.5.0 -> 0.5.1 everywhere it's asserted (`pyproject.toml`,
`src/gates/__init__.py`, `tests/test_smoke.py`, `uv.lock`). New test:
`tests/test_wheel_metadata.py` builds the wheel and asserts its METADATA
`Requires-Dist` for `agent-core` is exactly `agent-core<0.8,>=0.4.0`
(packaging's normalized order), never an `==` pin, and that the wheel
filename carries `0.5.1`.

## Why

T47 (decisions #207, #210, #219). The stale exact pin made it impossible to
ever declare a connectors wheel as a dependency of agent-core once agent-core
moved past 0.4.0 -- no version of connectors could satisfy an agent-core
install at 0.5+, which is the T47 install bug (`uv sync --offline` had to
drop the vendored connectors wheel because the lock didn't know about it,
seen 2026-09-28, s43 rig-service restart). Decision #219 (provisional,
orchestrator): connectors really imports agent-core
(`gates/secrets_port.py` -> `anorak.secrets`), so the requirement is
corrected, not dropped. Floor = the API this wheel is built on. Ceiling =
the next agent-core minor a connectors release hasn't been checked against,
raised only by a deliberate connectors release. This is connectors-side only
(T47 part 1, decision #210's two-PR order); agent-core declaring the wheels
as dependencies is a separate PR.

## Resolution proof

Scratch-only, nothing committed here or in `agent-core` (per decision #34,
provenance for any real re-vendor is a separate step):

- Built the 0.5.1 wheel into `/private/tmp/t47-proof/`.
- Copied `agent-core`'s `origin/main` (`746dca2`, version 0.7.28) via
  `git -C repos/agent-core archive origin/main | tar -x -C
  /private/tmp/t47-proof/agent-core` (no worktree, per instructions).
- Added `connectors==0.5.1` (source: the new wheel) and `playbooks==0.2.3`
  (source: agent-core's existing `vendor/playbooks-0.2.3-py3-none-any.whl`)
  to that copy's `[project.dependencies]` / `[tool.uv.sources]`.
- `uv lock` (offline and online, same result): **fails**, but only over
  `playbooks`, not `connectors`:

  ```
  error: No solution found when resolving dependencies
    cause: Because only playbooks==0.2.3 is available and playbooks==0.2.3
           depends on your project, we can conclude that all versions of
           playbooks depend on your project. And because your project
           depends on playbooks, we can conclude that your project's
           requirements are unsatisfiable.
  hint: The package `playbooks` depends on the package `agent-core` but the
        name is shadowed by your project. Consider changing the name of the
        project.
  ```

  `playbooks` 0.2.3's own metadata pins `agent-core==0.4.0` (agent-core's
  `vendor/PROVENANCE.md`, decision #61) -- unrelated to this connectors fix,
  and not a pin this PR touches. Isolated check: removing `playbooks` and
  locking with only `connectors==0.5.1` added **resolves cleanly** against
  the real agent-core 0.7.28 (`Resolved 44 packages`, `Added connectors
  v0.5.1`), which is the proof this PR's own claim needs -- the range this
  PR ships is satisfiable by a real, current agent-core version, unlike the
  old exact pin. The playbooks half of the pin-cycle is agent-core-repo
  territory (needs its own patch release, same shape as this one) and is out
  of scope for T47 part 1.

## Checks

<!-- swarm:checks -->

```
uv lock --offline -> Resolved 35 packages, Updated connectors v0.5.0 -> v0.5.1
uv run --offline pytest -q -> 669 passed
uv run --offline ruff check . -> All checks passed!
uv run --offline mypy --strict src scripts -> Success: no issues found in 22 source files
```

`ruff format --check` is not a CI step in this repo (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`
runs `ruff check .` only, no format step).

## Mutation check

- Mutant: revert `agent-core>=0.4.0,<0.8` back to `agent-core==0.4.0` in
  `pyproject.toml`. Killed by
  `tests/test_wheel_metadata.py::test_wheel_declares_agent_core_as_a_range_not_a_pin`
  (built wheel's `Requires-Dist` is `agent-core==0.4.0`, fails the
  `<0.8,>=0.4.0` assertion). Verified red on the pre-fix pyproject.
- Mutant: drop the ceiling, `agent-core>=0.4.0,<0.8` -> `agent-core>=0.4.0`.
  Killed by the same test (`str(specifier) == "<0.8,>=0.4.0"` is an exact
  match, not a substring/contains check, so a missing ceiling fails it too --
  verified directly: mutating just the ceiling away still fails that
  assertion, `1 failed, 1 passed`). No separate ceiling-only assertion was
  needed.
